title: Unveiling Prior-Data Fitted Networks on Causal Effect Estimation: Pre-Training or Fine-Tuning?
claim: Existing methods handle a single intervention, but under general interventions pre-training cannot cover the exponentially large interventional space, so unified estimation fails.
layout: 2 panels, left single vs right general, 3 numbered sub-boxes, bottom banners
description: A wide two-part figure. The left panel is titled 'Single Intervention'. It sets a green 'Causal Bayesian Perspective' column (Prior → RCT data/evidence → Posterior) beside a blue 'Prior-Fitted Networks Perspective' column. The PFN column shows small data tables flowing through a Pretrained PFN and a Predictive PFN, with in-context examples, inference arrows and a loss. A green check banner reads 'Unified Causal Effect Estimation (CEE)'. The right panel is titled 'General Intervention' and has three numbered boxes. (1) 'PFN Pre-training Process' is a left-to-right flow: all SCMs, then an exponential intervention space drawn as a galaxy image, then sampling, then distribution curves, then fitting. (2) 'Exponential Prior Uncoverage' is a dashed ellipse with covered and uncovered points, labelled Theorem 1. (3) 'Risk of PFNs Pre-trained with Interventional Data' is a red dashed box with TV divergence bounds, labelled Theorems 2 and 3. A red ✗ banner reads 'Impossible for Unified CEE'. The eye goes first to the two bold panel titles, then to the colored boxes.
caption: Left: Existing PFN-based causal foundation models on single intervention (treatment); Right: Our analysis on general
abstract: Amortized causal inference via Prior-data Fitted Networks (PFNs) has emerged as a promising paradigm, enabling zero-shot estimation of causal effects without the need for dataset-specific model tuning. However, the principled effectiveness of unified pre-training across general interventional regimes remains an underexplored question. In this paper, we investigate interventions on subsets of variables within Structural Causal Models (SCMs) and identify a fundamental theoretical limitation of current pre-training approaches. Theoretically, we prove that a single observational SCM induces an exponentially large space of interventional distributions, resulting in a phenomenon we term prior uncoverage. Consequently, this uncoverage yields a mismatch between the learned meta-prior and the true grounding prior, leading to unavoidable posterior inconsistency and estimation bias. To address this, we posit that fine-tuning is a fundamental necessity and propose a target-specific strategy named Point-Wise Interventional Fine-tuning (PWF), enabling the local generalization property. We further scale this approach via Meta-Sampling Fine-tuning (MSF) from a budgeted active learning perspective, thereby achieving uniform generalization on any interventional distribution.
